issues.description: Method messageOnMilk: the problem statement contains two conflicting specifications. In the UML/interface section (problem_statement.md) the method is declared as messageOnMilk(): String (no parameters), but in Part 2 prose the text states messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) and describes a return string including the volume. The template Main.java calls messageOnMilk() with no argument, and the solution's Milkable.java defines String messageOnMilk() (no parameter). This discrepancy leaves students unsure whether to implement the interface method with a double parameter (which would not match the provided template/solution and would cause compilation or test failures) or without parameters (which contradicts the Part 2 description that mentions the milkVolume).
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method signature across all artifacts. Preferred quick resolution: update the problem statement Part 2 text to describe messageOnMilk() with no parameters and remove references to milkVolume (so it matches the UML, template Main, and solution). Alternatively, if the intent is to teach method parameters, update the UML, the Milkable interface (solution and template), and all example calls to use messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) and adjust expected return strings and tests to include the volume. Ensure the problem statement, template code, and solution/tests consistently use the same signature.
